transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-28 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Bui (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CyanWave Head of ML), Ethan Ruiz (CTO), Sofia Gomez (Platform)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time for us, um, really excited to dig in. Quick check on audio — can you hear us ok?
[00:10] Priya: Yeah yep, sounds good. Thanks Lena.
[00:20] Lena: Cool. Marcus and I will take you through model choices and runtime options, then we'll switch to the technical side for Marcus to riff on benchmarks and KV cache stuff.
[00:30] Ethan: High level for us — we do automated highlight reels from multi-hour broadcast recordings, so we need strong summarization with entities preserved, sometimes in Spanish, Portuguese and Hindi. Typical input is 45 to 90 minutes of speech, post-transcribed to text. We're seeing bursts of long context, so the 20k to 32k token range is, uh, where we live.
[00:50] Marcus: Got it. So when you say 45 to 90 minutes, is that pre-segmentation? Do you chunk at speaker changes or send as single long prompt?
[01:05] Priya: We currently chunk heuristically, but want to move to a single-pass summarization to avoid coherence loss. So ideally a single context window that can hold the sequence or at least effective KV caching between segments.
[01:20] Marcus: Right, that maps to two approaches: large-context models (native 32k) or continuous prefix caching and stitching with a shorter model. Both have cost/latency tradeoffs. Redwood supports both on the runtime side — continuous batching and KV cache reuse is something we tune for you.
[01:40] Sofia: Quick question on tool-calling — we need structured metadata extraction (speaker timestamps, named entities, ad-break markers) and will likely rely on tool calls to our microservices. How mature is the tool-calling path?
[01:55] Marcus: We have function-style tool-calling and you can attach external callouts. There are a couple of caveats — streaming + tool-calls adds complexity for ordering and retries — our runtime handles ordered callbacks but you'll want idempotent endpoints. Also tooling name mangling sometimes shows up in ASR-to-LLM pipelines, so expect a little debug.
[02:20] Lena: And on deployment: you mentioned compliance constraints, Ethan?
[02:25] Ethan: Yes, for enterprise customers we need SOC2 and SAML SSO, and some clients require a VPC-backed deployment or on-prem for raw audio storage. Data residency is a factor for EU customers.
[02:38] Lena: Redwood has hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem. Hosted is fastest to try, Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and predictable throughput, Private gives customer-managed control plane for the strictest compliance.
[02:52] Priya: Our initial thought is Dedicated — we want predictable throughput for nightly batch jobs but also the option to burst for live highlights. We also want to test 32k context quality.
[03:05] Marcus: For 32k context we can onboard models like LlamaX-32k variant or Mistral-long if you want open weights, or a quantized 32k variant to reduce costs. There is a quality delta between native long-context models and stitching — sometimes subtle hallucination around entity continuity.
[03:25] Priya: Any recommendations on open models? We're trying to avoid closed APIs for cost and data control.
[03:31] Marcus: If you want community/open models, Llama-derivatives (Llama2-extended, LlamaX) and Mistral long are good starting points. Mistral fine-tuned long-context variants show good summarization. But you should run evals — we can help with a prompt-suite. Also note Anthropic-like models sometimes do better on instruction-constrain but are closed.
[03:55] Ethan: How about latency? Nightly batches are fine with higher latency, but our live highlight path needs sub-2s per segment end-to-end.
[04:03] Marcus: Sub-2s is achievable on Dedicated with smaller context for per-segment calls and aggressive batching off-path. For 32k single-pass, latency will increase — typically token throughput slows. We can route live traffic to lighter-weight variants and batch the heavy summarization jobs to Dedicated GPUs.
[04:25] Sofia: Can Redwood route requests by policy? Like live low-latency to hosted cheap model and fallback to Dedicated if it drops?
[04:33] Lena: Yes that's called smart routing — you can set policies by latency, cost, region. We also support automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained.
[04:45] Priya: Ok cool. Also curious about quantization — what's the quality tradeoff if we quantize a large open model to int8 or 4-bit?
[04:55] Marcus: In many cases int8 preserves generation quality very well, 4-bit can be fine but depends on the model architecture and the prompts. For entity-sensitive summaries you may notice a small drop in rare-entity fidelity. Redwood Optimize will give recommendations per workload.
[05:15] Ethan: Security — KMS integration for keys, do you support customer-managed keys or HSM?
[05:21] Lena: Yes, Private and Dedicated support KMS integrations; Private can plug into your HSM for encryption-at-rest, and we capture audit logs. We'll share the security whitepaper.
[05:33] Priya: On evals — we'd like you to run a benchmark using our 500 sample clips with ground-truth annotations to compare models on ROUGE/ROUGE-L and entity recall.
[05:44] Marcus: That's perfect. If you share the sample prompts and expected outputs, we'll spin up a benchmark on Dedicated and include Mistral-long, LlamaX-32k, and a quantized Llama variant.
[05:55] Ethan: Timeline — we want to kick a pilot in early March if possible.
[06:00] Lena: We can target 2028-03-05 for a 1-week pilot window. I'll send the pricing and contract draft for the Dedicated pilot.
[06:08] Sofia: Do you have any docs on cost per token for large context? We need to model nightly cost.
[06:14] Marcus: We'll share unit economics — bigger context increases effective per-token cost but caching and prefix reuse can reduce it. We'll include sample cost curves in the pricing sheet.
[06:26] Priya: A little worried about transcription noise — our ASR sometimes splits speakers wrong, which can confuse models. Is speaker-aware context handling something you support?
[06:36] Marcus: Yes we have structured input support (speaker tags) and token-level metadata. Feeding speaker tags consistently helps the model. Also you can do reranking on the Redwood runtime to prefer continuity.
[06:50] Ethan: Any limitations on tool-calling throughput? If we're making many microservice calls per document, could that create a bottleneck?
[06:58] Marcus: The runtime does support high throughput calls but you'll want to design for idempotency and backpressure. We recommend batching tool-calls where sensible and doing async callbacks.
[07:10] Priya: On multilingual — do open models handle Portuguese/Hindi well out of the box? We may need fine-tuning.
[07:18] Marcus: Many open models are better in European languages; for Hindi you might see degraded quality. We recommend a small, targeted fine-tune or synthetic data augmentation. Redwood can help estimate costs for fine-tuning vs prompt engineering.
[07:34] Lena: Quick break out — Marcus, can you explain KV cache reuse strategy and how it impacts cost?
[07:40] Marcus: Sure. KV caching stores past key/value attention states so you don't re-compute bulk of earlier tokens. For segmented workflows, you can cache prefixes and reuse them, so effective compute per new token drops. This saves cost and lowers latency for subsequent segments. However cache size matters for memory, and native long-context models avoid some complexity but at higher GPU RAM.
[08:10] Ethan: If we do Dedicated reserved capacity, do we get autoscale/burst options for peaks?
[08:16] Lena: Yes Dedicated offers configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity for spikes, subject to contract terms. You can set a baseline reserved and an on-demand burst pool.
[08:27] Priya: For compliance with EU data residency, can we pin a region and ensure logs/audit stay there?
[08:34] Lena: Private gives you the most control; Dedicated can be region-pinned as well. We'll map the options in the security doc.
[08:42] Sofia: A few smaller items — do you support SAML/SSO + RBAC for dev teams?
[08:48] Lena: Yes SAML SSO and RBAC with token-level controls are supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports enterprise SSO for account control but Private gives most isolation.
[08:59] Priya: Any customer stories for media workflows?
[09:03] Marcus: We worked with a streaming partner on highlight generation — they used a hybrid approach: small model for live cues and Dedicated 32k for nightly summarization. That reduced costs and preserved latency for live features.
[09:17] Ethan: Sounds like a reasonable path. Priya — any other blockers?
[09:22] Priya: We'll want the benchmark, cost sheet, and security docs. Also an initial throughput SLA for the pilot.
[09:30] Lena: We'll include an SLA for the pilot, but formal SLA comes with reserved contracts.
[09:36] Marcus: For benchmarks we'll need your sample prompts and ground truth; also define metrics: latency, ROUGE, entity recall, and false positive hallucination rates.
[09:48] Priya: I'll get those over by Friday.
[09:52] Ethan: One more thing — how do you handle model rollouts and version pinning? We can't have nightly changes break downstream systems.
[10:00] Lena: You can pin model versions per-route and use canary rollouts with automatic fallback. Redwood Console gives per-route dashboards and rollout controls.
[10:12] Sofia: Great. Any cost-savings levers?
[10:15] Marcus: Batching, prefix caching, quantization, and model routing (route cheaper variants for non-critical tasks) are the main levers. We can show a configuration that meets your budget.
[10:30] Priya: Ok I think we have enough. Recap of next steps?
[10:36] Lena: We'll send the pricing/pilot contract, security docs, and the benchmark plan. Marcus will start the benchmark template and request the sample set. We set pilot start target 2028-03-05.
[10:48] Ethan: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[10:52] Priya: Thanks.
[10:55] Lena: Appreciate the time. We'll follow up with notes and the documents.
[11:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: Some ASR artifacts and proper-noun spelling variance (model names like LlamaX, Mistral-long, and internal features) may be slightly off.
